Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Serum vitamin D was independently associated with lower odds of post-stroke depression.
Sentence: "Vitamin D was independently associated with PSD (OR 0.95, 95% CI 0.935-0.966, P < 0.001)."
Measured as: post-stroke depression
Population: 402 acute stroke patients
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (observational, measured)
Comparator: Higher vs lower vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 402
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

{
  "rationale": "Study B investigates vitamin C supplementation rather than vitamin D, making this pair off-question.",
